tob-10813: Written just before his conversion to Catholicism, Newman’s famous essay argues that Christian doctrine was not fixed once and for all but grew and deepened across the centuries — like a seed becoming a tree. This idea of ‘development’ helped him justify joining the Catholic Church. The essay remains one of the most important works of modern Christian theology.
tob-0213: G. K. Chesterton’s nightmare-farce trails the poet-detective Syme into a ring of anarchists — each named for a weekday — in a chase that turns the world head over heels. Half thriller, half God-joke, it ends as a plea for wonder over despair. The book is Chesterton at his merriest and deepest.
tob-9047-61113: The fourth volume of Pliny’s Natural History treats cures drawn from beasts — and the wonder-working, old wives’ lore, and quackery tangled with them. It is the old world’s medicine chest, gripping and gruesome by turns. Bostock’s English keeps every strange receipt.
tob-4113: Max Müller’s first Upanishad volume opened the Sacred Books of the East series itself — the Chandogya and fellow early Upanishads in English dress. His rendering and notes grounded Veda-study in the western world. Victorian readers met the All-One and the Self for the first time. The volume is a monument of learning.
tob-12913: Annie Besant’s Ancient Wisdom — 1897 — is the classic popular Theosophy text, summarizing the Secret Doctrine’s vast cosmic system. Her clear exposition made Theosophy accessible to thousands of readers. The book remains the best general introduction to the movement.
tob-0039-d13: This microfilm roll carries a piece of the Doctors’ Trial record at Nuremberg — the official account of the Nazi doctors’ trial. Proof, exhibits, and rulings stand here in full. Every page serves the historical record. Scholars prize the whole set for its fullness.
cia-0000109013: Soviet Forced Labor: An Update, dated November 1985 — another in the series of periodic refreshers the CIA produced on the camp system. Each update folded new camp reports into the standing picture for policymakers. The repetition is the story: year after year, the forced-labor machine kept running, and Washington kept watching.
cia-0000112813: An untitled supplementary report dated January 1945 — the archive's spelling says supplmentary. Wartime files are full of such addenda: extra pages attached to a main report, now separated from it. The entry is a loose thread from the war's intelligence tapestry, its parent document lost to the filing system.
cia-0000119213: A November 1982 notice of priority change number six — bureaucratic, but priorities are how intelligence agencies say what matters most. Shifting a collection priority meant moving spies, satellites, and analysts to a new target. The entry is a gear-shift in the machinery, its destination unstated.
cia-0000119713: A May 1953 estimate of probable developments in Indonesia. Sukarno's young republic was fracturing along regional and ideological lines. The document forecasts a sprawling archipelago nation whose troubles would only deepen through the decade.
cia-0000124313: A July 1951 report, its title carrying the archive's typo, on communist treatment of United Nations prisoners. How captors treated prisoners was both a humanitarian concern and a propaganda battleground. The document gathers the evidence — the charges that would echo through the armistice talks.
cia-0000132213: Situation Report 530: Baghdad radio calling for something — the truncated title cuts off the appeal. Iraqi propaganda broadcasts were monitored word by word for shifts in tone. The document is the war heard through the enemy's own loudspeaker.
cia-0000132413: An October 1959 assessment of the possibility that Castro's government would break relations with the United States. The rupture was coming — the only question was when. The document weighs the break: the hemisphere's divorce, foretold.
cia-0000132513: An April 1961 preliminary assessment of the consequences for America of the abortive attack on Castro's regime — the Bay of Pigs, days away or just past. Someone was already counting the cost of failure. The document is the morning after, anticipated: the disaster, foreseen.
cia-0000132613: Item 4 in the July 1960 series: Haiti seeking rapprochement with Cuba. Papa Doc's Haiti wanted better ties with revolutionary Havana — strange bedfellows. The document is the courtship: the dictatorship, wooing the revolution.
cia-0000135813: A 1954 general file on political action — conversations deleted — with specific debriefings, the truncated title suggests. The politics and the interrogations, together. The entry is the double file: the persuasion and the questioning.
cia-0000135913: A 1954 report — author deleted — of meetings with undisclosed persons, given changed circumstances, the truncated title suggests. The situation shifted; the meetings adapted. The entry is the adjustment: the talks, re-targeted.
cia-0000136113: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reviewing a report that suggested playing the waiting game. Patience as strategy, debated. The document is the review: the waiting, weighed.
cia-0000136313: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reporting a summary of RO material from 1400 to 2300 — the truncated title cuts off the date. The afternoon and evening take. The entry is the summary: the hours, covered.
un-ga-res-a-69-13: General Assembly Resolution A/69/13, adopted in 2014. The thirteenth act. The entry is the record: the number, the year — the rest, the text's.
un-ga-res-13: UN General Assembly Resolution 13, from 1946 — the thirteenth act in UN history. The first session's early days. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-113: Security Council Resolution 113, adopted in 1956. The Suez year's Council. The number and year endure; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-713: Security Council Resolution 713, adopted in September 1991 — the Yugoslavia arms embargo, imposed as the federation broke apart. The Council tried to starve the coming wars of weapons. The resolution is the embargo: the arms, cut off.
un-sc-res-1913: Security Council Resolution 1913, cataloged with the year 2007 — the numbering suggests 2010, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
cia-0000135613: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135613. The invaders' own documents, in Spanish. The entry is the archive: the brigade, on paper.
cia-0000135713: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135713. The papers of the defeated invasion. The document is the defeat's paper: the brigade, after.
cia-0000136613: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136613. The Bay of Pigs brigade's papers. The document is the brigade's: the papers, Spanish.
cia-0000136713: An estimated 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136713, date approximate. The circa pre-invasion set. The entry is the circa: the year, about 1960.
plos-pone-0000013: A 2006 PLOS ONE study of the short- and long-term effects of hVEGF-A 165 in Cre-activated transgenic mice — the truncated title cuts off the rest. A blood-vessel growth factor, switched on by genetic trickery, and its consequences. The paper is the experiment: the growth factor, activated.
cia-0000137313: A 1960 CIA briefing for the National Security Council on Cuba — number 0000137313. The council heard the island's file. The entry is the hearing: the briefing, delivered.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d13: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, June 28, 1943 — Document 13. Washington answered London. The message is the answer: the president, replying.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d113: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 10, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 113. London answered the same day. The message is the quickness: the reply, immediate.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d213: A report by the Joint Staff Planners — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 213. The planners' assessment. The report is the planning: the staff, assessing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d313: A memorandum by the British Chiefs of Staff, November 25, 1943 — Document 313. The British planners' paper. The memo is the paper: the chiefs, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d413: The Secretary of State to the ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 413. The department wrote Moscow's envoy. The memo is the envoy: Harriman, instructed.
arxiv-2605-08913: Running a language model on a Mac should get faster as you shrink the workload — but sometimes it does not. Willy Fitra and Hendria document non-monotonic latency in Apple MPS decoding, tracing the hiccups to interactions between the KV cache and the chip's execution regimes. The 2026 paper is performance forensics for Apple-silicon inference.
arxiv-2605-09113: Real storage media forbid certain patterns — and still demand error correction. Prachi Mishra, Sidharth Jaggi, Navin Kashyap, and colleagues construct error-correcting codes under weak constraints, pinning down the achievable rates. The 2026 paper is coding theory for the messy realities of physical storage.
arxiv-2605-09313: Diffusion transformers develop attention sinks — tokens that hog attention for no clear reason, warping the generation. Fangzheng Wu and Brian Summa analyze them causally, asking what creates the sinks and what they do to outputs. The 2026 paper is interpretability research for generative transformers.
arxiv-2605-09413: Saying the right words in the wrong tone ruins the message — expressive appropriateness matters. Tianrui Wang, Ziyang Ma, Yizhou Peng, and colleagues evaluate it for speech in rich contexts. The 2026 paper judges not what voices say, but how fittingly they say it.
arxiv-2605-09513: Long-horizon trackers drift — slowly losing their target — and need semantic watchdogs. Mayank Anand, Mohammad Saqlain, Kyan Mahajan, and Priya Shukla propose QueST: persistent queries as semantic monitors for drift suppression. The 2026 paper keeps trackers honest over the long haul.
arxiv-2605-09713: Rare-earth nickelates hide a non-magnetic insulating phase born from the Jahn-Teller effect — lattice distortions that split electron orbitals. Sangeeta Rajpurohit, Liang Z. Tan, Tadashi Ogitsu, and colleagues investigate it in RNiO3. The 2026 paper is condensed-matter physics on correlated oxides.
arxiv-2605-10013: LLMs infer personas from user data — but when is that inference acceptable? Kyzyl Monteiro, Minjung Park, Alexander Ioffrida, and colleagues study user reactions and control preferences for inferred personas. The 2026 paper is human-computer interaction on the acceptability of being profiled.
arxiv-2605-10113: Motzkin paths with two variants of level steps on odd levels, counted via the classical kernel method. Helmut Prodinger develops the enumeration carefully. The 2026 paper is enumerative combinatorics. It counts exotic lattice paths with precise kernel-method machinery. A masterclass in enumeration.
plos-pone-0003413: Wildlife immunologists went looking for immune tissue in shrews in this 2008 study. Studying how wild animals fight their native parasites is key to understanding immunity outside the lab, so the team mapped the blood-forming and immune tissues of the European common shrew. Their survey grounds future work on how small mammals defend themselves in the wild.
plos-pone-0003513: Bee researchers caught scent memories interfering in this 2008 learning study. Restrained honey bees extend their proboscis to learned odors, and the team found that backward pairing, odor after reward, creates inhibitory interference with new learning. The olfactory clash reveals how the bee brain untangles competing scent associations.
plos-pone-0003613: Cell biologists Liesa, Borda-d'Água, and Medina-Gómez found a master switch for mitochondrial merging in this 2008 paper. The nuclear coactivator PGC-1beta increased mitochondrial fusion, tipping the balance away from fragmentation. The result ties gene regulation in the nucleus to the shape-shifting dynamics of the cell's power plants.
plos-pone-0003713: In 2008, Schmidt, Stark, and Wilson set quality checks for deep-sequencing libraries. ChIP-seq, which maps where proteins grip DNA, is only as good as its input libraries. Their genome-scale validation gives labs a way to certify libraries before burning money on a full sequencing run.
plos-pone-0003813: Edwards, Fridley, and James tightened the rules for gene-hunt replication in this 2008 paper. Their evaluation of clustering and genotype distribution gives genome-wide association studies a better way to confirm hits. The methods raise the bar for claiming a gene-disease link.
plos-pone-0003913: In 2008, Dushek, Mueller, and Soubies watched immune receptors roam the cell surface. Using fluorescence recovery, they measured how the T-cell receptor moves under different calcium and actin states. Both the calcium level and the actin skeleton tuned the receptor's mobility. The result links the cell's inner scaffolding to how its sensors patrol.
plos-pone-0004013: In 2008, Wei, Qing, and Ye coaxed stem cells toward making eggs and sperm. They drove embryonic stem cells to specify primordial germ cells in a dish. Primordial germ cell specification is the crucial first step toward the germ line. The lab-dish system opens germ-cell beginnings to direct experimental study.
plos-pone-0004113: In 2009, Xu, Bae, and Zhang watched cells build their scaffolding. Display of fibronectin assembly sites on cell surfaces shifted with each adherence. Cells stuck to varied coatings exposed uneven docking sites fast. The neat finding maps how grip shapes construction.
plos-pone-0004213: In 2009, Kelly, Karsten, and Geschwind compared stem cells by address. Cultured spinal cord neural stem cells kept their regional identity. Brain-derived stem cells differed in lineage character. The address stamped the cells' behavior. The finding guides matching donor cells to spinal injuries.
plos-pone-0004313: In 2009, Lapidus, Minetti, and Djibo counted the human cost of hunger. Mortality risk among 68,001 malnourished children in Niger's 2006 feeding program was mapped. The huge cohort revealed who died and why clearly. The stark data sharpen famine response planning today greatly.
plos-pone-0357713: Standard eye charts use bold black letters — but real life is gray on gray. This study measured low-contrast visual acuity in healthy adults and examined its impact in non-pathologic myopia. The results show what nearsighted people lose in everyday, low-contrast vision that the big-E chart never catches.
plos-pone-0357813: Tracking a moving target through clutter defeats simple algorithms. This paper extended a target tracking algorithm with trajectory feedback constraining spatial information. The feedback loop steadies the track when measurements get noisy — useful for radar, sonar, and surveillance systems that cannot afford to lose the plot.
plos-pone-0353613: Counting child deaths in India demands methods that work with patchy, incomplete data. This population-based cross-sectional study developed an indirect technique to estimate neonatal, infant, and under-five mortality for India and its states. The method hands policymakers credible state-by-state numbers to act on.
plos-pone-0340713: Should governments mandate open-sourcing in tiers to spur innovation? This differential game study asked whether tiered open-source mandates optimize innovation, modeling platform versus independent project dynamics in software ecosystems. The game-theoretic results give policymakers a rigorous basis for software regulation.
plos-pone-0357313: Reading ability may predict how well we understand other minds. This study showed literacy predicts performance on a second-order false-belief task — the classic test of theory of mind. The link connects the mechanics of reading with the deeper human skill of understanding what others think.
plos-pone-0355313: Chimpanzees speak in regional dialects — and infants must learn them. This paper studied the ontogeny of dialects across chimpanzee vocalisations, tracing how young apes acquire their group’s accent. The developmental story reveals genuine culture unfolding in the wild.
plos-pone-0357413: PhD supervisors make or break the doctoral experience — and now there’s global data to prove it. This paper used the Nature Careers 2025 Global PhD Survey to show how supervisor support shapes PhD students’ learning experience. The worldwide evidence demands better, more accountable supervision.
plos-pone-0357213: ADHD risk screening could improve dramatically by combining brain data with life context. This paper integrated socioeconomic context with multimodal EEG data for improved ADHD risk screening. The fusion of signals sharpens detection beyond what either source achieves alone.
plos-pone-0355713: Can artificial intelligence genuinely help children become more independent? This qualitative analysis explored pre-service teachers’ views on using AI in special education. The future teachers’ perspectives — hopeful, wary, practical — will shape how AI actually enters classrooms.
plos-pone-0356813: Children born with Hirschsprung’s disease or anorectal malformations need lifelong follow-up. The Colorectal Centre of Excellence Registry protocol establishes a prospective longitudinal cohort to track them. The registry will generate the long-term outcome data these families and surgeons desperately need.
plos-pone-0351713: Impostor phenomenon — feeling like a fraud despite evident competence — may be endemic in medical training. This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated its global prevalence among medical students. The pooled numbers reveal just how many future doctors secretly doubt they belong.
plos-pone-0357013: Satellites and ground stations must share the airwaves without stepping on each other. This paper analyzed the performance of RSMA-enabled satellite-terrestrial communication networks — rate-splitting multiple access tying space and earth together. The performance analysis shows how this clever spectrum-sharing scheme squeezes more capacity from the same scarce frequencies.
plos-pone-0354513: Coal shearer cable test machines need height-adjustment mechanisms that are both strong and light. This paper applied topology optimization — letting mathematics carve away unneeded material — to design one. The optimized mechanism delivers the required strength with minimal weight, improving the test rig’s performance.
plos-pone-0355113: Cancer treatment ends — but survivors’ needs don’t. This in-depth qualitative study captured the perceptions of cancer survivors and healthcare professionals on what adequate supportive care after treatment really looks like. The converging and diverging views point to a survivorship care model built on listening.
plos-pone-0355613: Neural networks learn better with activation functions that adapt their shape. This paper developed adaptive activation functions with curvature and range modulation for abstract image feature learning in complex CNNs for cross-domain applications. The flexible activations help networks transfer learning across visual domains more effectively.
plos-pone-0356013: The thickness of a chewing muscle — visible on scans — might predict immunotherapy success. This paper associated temporal muscle thickness with immunotherapy outcomes in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The simple imaging marker could help oncologists identify who’ll benefit from these expensive drugs.
plos-pone-0329913: Nailfold capillaries — tiny vessels at the fingernail base — reveal systemic disease. The CAPoxy feasibility study investigated multispectral imaging in nailfold capillaroscopy. The novel imaging approach could turn a simple nail examination into a window on oxygenation and microvascular health.
plos-pone-0354913: Ethiopia’s Abaya-Chamo sub-basin faces shifting hydroclimatic trends and deepening drought. This paper examined those trends for climate resilience in the Rift Valley Lake Basin’s eastern escarpment. The findings give water managers the long view needed to plan for a drier future.
plos-pone-0355413: Bacterial and fungal infections strike differently by sex, age, and season — patterns worth mapping. This paper characterized those distribution characteristics. The epidemiological mapping helps clinicians anticipate what’s coming through the door — and when.
europmc-pmc2807913: Plants sense drought through the hormone abscisic acid, and this 2010 paper fills in a missing link in that chain. The authors identify PYR/PYL/RCAR family proteins as the main partners of the ABI1 phosphatase inside living Arabidopsis cells. Pinning down these interactions clarifies how the drought signal gets through. The finding advanced efforts to breed more drought-tolerant crops.
europmc-pmc2826413: The Parkinson's-tied protein DJ-1 guards the cell's power packs. This 2010 paper shows that losing DJ-1 cuts the cell's self-cleaning and wrecks power-pack upkeep. The team traces how its loss lets harm pile up. The work ties one gene to the cell faults behind Parkinson's.
europmc-pmc2831913: Air pollution does not hit men and women identically. This 2010 paper argues for a growing role of gender analysis in air pollution epidemiology. The author reviews why sex and gender matter in exposure and health effects. The call pushed researchers to stop treating gender as an afterthought in pollution studies.
europmc-pmc2852313: Coot lets researchers build and fix protein models by hand on screen, turning raw X-ray data into finished structures. This 2010 paper tours the tool's traits and growth, from its first release to wide adoption. The authors chart how it won its users with speed and a friendly design. The write-up marks the rise of a lab staple that many crystallographers still open daily.
europmc-pmc2855713: Green tea compounds are tested against cancer cells with color-change assays, but this 2010 paper warns the tests can lie. The authors show MTT and MTS assays misread the anti-growth effects of green tea polyphenols. Their caution matters because false readings waste research. The paper taught tea researchers to distrust a popular shortcut.
europmc-pmc2891813: Malaria persists in Brazil's vast terrain, and this 2010 paper surveys the fight. The authors give an overview of malaria in Brazil, its patterns and control. Their synthesis aids a large country's campaign. The review is a reference for Latin American malaria.
europmc-pmc2930213: White blood cells live fast and die young, and this 2010 review tracks them. The authors cover neutrophil life cycles in health and disease. Their overview follows the short, fierce life of a front-line defender. The review helps doctors read immune cell counts.
europmc-pmc2936113: Memory runs on brain highways, and this 2010 paper maps two key ones. The authors uncover direct and indirect pathways linking the hippocampus to the anterior thalamus for memory. Their wiring diagram explains how recall travels. The work guides memory research and its disorders.
europmc-pmc2936313: The pregnancy hormone hCG does more than turn tests positive. This 2010 review covers the many jobs of hCG and its kin molecules in the body. The author's tour spans womb, ovary, and beyond. Their review clarifies what a famous hormone really does.
europmc-pmc3000813: Blood chemistry mirrors blood sugar control. This 2010 study charts blood chemistry in obese Black women with and without diabetes. The authors reveal the metabolic signature. Their work points to early markers. The signature differs sharply between the groups. Doctors may spot risk before sugar spikes.
europmc-pmc3017113: Insect-killing fungi got their genomes read. This 2011 paper sequences two Metarhizium fungi and compares their active genes. The authors reveal the killers' toolkit. Their work aids green pesticides. The fungi punch through insect armor. Farmers spray spores instead of chemicals.
europmc-pmc3053313: The brain learns from movement mistakes. This 2011 paper shows the brain uses surprise signals to tune reaching movements. The authors reveal the error codes. Their work informs robots and rehab. Reward sweetens the learning signal. Stroke patients relearn reach with these cues.
europmc-pmc6515513: BNP and NT-proBNP are hormones the heart releases when it strains, and doctors already use blood levels to diagnose heart failure. This review makes a second case: the same markers can help forensic pathologists judge whether a deceased person's heart was failing. Covering both clinic and morgue, it shows how one blood test serves the living and explains the dead.
europmc-pmc6568213: Antibodies do more than grab targets - their tail ends rally immune attack, and small tweaks change how long they linger in blood. This review covers the design ideas for tuning antibody effector functions and stretching circulation half-life. The concepts guide engineers building longer-lasting, harder-hitting antibody drugs.
europmc-pmc6632213: Head and neck squamous cell cancers kill some 380,000 people a year worldwide. This consensus statement from the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer lays out how immunotherapy fits their treatment: which patients benefit, what the evidence shows, and where the field goes next. Expert guidance for a common, cruel cancer.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-113: GAO's 2007 report grades the guard plans written for banks, power grids, and other must-run sectors — and finds the cyber parts wildly uneven. Some plans faced the hacker threat head-on; others barely waved at it. The report shows a nation defending its lifelines with a patchwork shield, strong in spots and tissue-thin in others.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-13: GAO's 2007 report looks at the Navy's mine hunters — ships, choppers, and sub drones that sweep sea mines. The gear held real promise, GAO found, but only if the Navy licked its build and fielding troubles. The report covers a quiet, vital mission: keeping the sea lanes open against one of war's cheapest killers.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-913: Homeland Security's money hygiene was poor in 2007, GAO found — the young department lagged at sizing up wrong payments and clawing them back. The report grades DHS against the clean-books law Congress wrote for every agency. The verdict: a security giant still learning to count its own change.
gao-gaoreports-b-297800-13: INDUS Technology took its June 2007 contract dispute to GAO — thirteenth round in a long docket — and this ruling is the call. The firm challenged the award; the ruling tests the claims. Long-running bid sagas still get a careful, final answer.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-513: The island trust funds were running dry in 2007 — GAO's report warns the Micronesian and Marshallese nest eggs might not last. The findings do the long math on the compacts' money. The report's question hangs over the Pacific: what happens when the trust runs out?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-713: Biofuels were booming without a map in 2007 — GAO's report says the Energy Department lacked a strategy to match rising production with pipes and pumps. The findings expose the infrastructure gap. The report's warning: fuel nobody can move is fuel nobody can burn.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-213: Social Security's rescue math needed sunlight in 2007, and GAO's report says the public deserved clearer numbers on general-revenue financing. The findings demand real transparency from the trustees. The report's creed is simple: the retirement promise should be priced in the open, not in the dark.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-113: Biodefense planning needed clearer orders in 2007, and GAO's report says updated intelligence, clear guidance, and steady priorities were required. The findings demand the direction. The report warns that the germ-war shield needed a real strategy. The priorities had to hold.
openalex-w7207867013: Can practicing on actors make medical students more caring doctors? Researchers at a medical school in western Parana, Brazil, measured students' empathy before and after simulated patient consultations, practice visits with trained stand-ins. Using a before-and-after design, the study tests whether rehearsal builds the human side of medicine. The result speaks to a simple idea: empathy can be taught, and practice is how.
openalex-w7205009213: What happens to mining engineers after graduation? This study tracks 548 graduates of the Federal University of Ouro Preto from 2013 to 2023, drawing on surveys of 125 alumni plus faculty records. The picture is tough: new graduates face outsized demands for prior experience, software skills, and English, and nearly half of jobs come through personal contacts. A data-rich reality check on the path from engineering degree to mining job.
openalex-w7205013813: Septic shock is the deadliest face of sepsis, and survival depends on speed. This literature review surveys current strategies for the early management of septic shock: recognizing it fast and acting immediately. The authors synthesize what intensive care research says about the measures that save lives in the first critical hours. A clinical review where the takeaway is blunt, in septic shock, delay kills.
pmc-13472513: In this 2026 qualitative study, frontline nurse managers at a private hospital share their views on person-centered management — leadership that treats staff as individuals with their own needs. The paper reports what works, what falls short, and how management style affects nurses' daily work. It gives hospital administrators firsthand insight into managing care teams humanely.
pmc-13492213: A 2026 cardiology paper showing that vectorcardiography — a 3D view of the heart's electrical activity — reflects left ventricular reverse remodeling after cardiac resynchronization therapy, for both left bundle branch area pacing and biventricular pacing. The electrical signal tracks the heart's structural recovery. It offers a simple tool for monitoring therapy.
pmc-13439313: A 2026 cardiology paper comparing hemolysis — red blood cell destruction — and kidney effects across different pulsed field ablation systems for atrial fibrillation. Pulsed field ablation is the new energy source for heart rhythm procedures, and device differences matter. The head-to-head comparison guides system choice.
pmc-13416013: This 2026 microbiology paper proposes mechanisms for the first step of anaerobic benzene degradation — how bacteria break down benzene without oxygen — presumably involving a flavoprotein. Benzene is a stubborn pollutant, and the initial attack is the hardest step. The work illuminates a key bioremediation pathway.
pmc-13385513: A 2026 education paper on using simple phantoms — physical models — to teach diagnostic and radiation therapy principles in hands-on medical physics outreach. Cheap, tangible models make abstract physics click for students. The paper shares designs and lessons from outreach events.
pmc-13348013: A 2026 neuroimaging paper using automated surface-based segmentation of deep gray matter regions from diffusion tensor images to reveal unique age trajectories across the healthy lifespan. Deep brain structures age on their own schedules. The normative curves give clinicians a reference for abnormal aging.
pmc-13482513: This 2026 implementation study examined factors in rolling out ASH sickle cell disease guidelines on silent cerebral infarcts and cognition at a single sickle cell center. Guidelines only help if adopted. The single-center analysis shows what implementation takes.
pmc-13267413: A 2026 (listed as 2025 in the record) paper on calibrated dietary patterns and cancer risk in the Women's Health Initiative cohorts. Diet measurement error plagues nutrition science; calibration corrects it. The calibrated analysis gives cleaner risk estimates.
pmc-13525913: A 2026 paper on automatic frequent measurements of plasma sodium, potassium, carbon dioxide, urea nitrogen, and other values during hemodialysis. Real-time chemistry during dialysis enables tighter control. The automation is the advance.
pmc-13450513: This 2026 radiology paper assessed left main coronary artery stenosis on coronary CT angiography. The widow-maker lesion needs accurate non-invasive assessment. The paper evaluates CT's performance.
pmc-13424313: A 2026 ecology paper asking whether there are choices in the darkness — habitat selection and environmental filtering shaping invertebrate communities in semi-arid caves. Cave life isn't random. The study reveals the assembly rules.
pmc-13574513: A 2026 study of periodontal status and oral health-related quality of life among postmenopausal women at an Indian tertiary government hospital. Gum disease affects daily life. The study quantifies the burden in this population.
pmc-13529113: This 2026 neurology paper addressed poststroke fever etiology — what causes fever after stroke. The differential diagnosis matters for treatment. The paper organizes the causes.
pmc-13499013: A 2026 Alzheimer's paper dissecting the proteomic landscape through NULISA profiling of brain cell-specific extracellular vesicles. The vesicles carried cell-type-specific protein signatures. The profiling is the advance.
pmc-13648013: In this 2026 zebrafish paper, knockout models of atxn1a, atxn1b, and atxn1l revealed distinct and shared phenotypic and transcriptomic alterations. The ataxia genes' fish models were compared. The alterations inform neurodegeneration.
pmc-13454313: This 2026 chemistry paper applied the hydrogen-bond-mediated aglycone delivery reaction to synthesizing alpha- and beta-linked 2-azido-2-deoxyglucosides. The glycosylation method was the advance. The application expands synthesis.
pmc-13446413: A 2026 philosophy paper on intellectual humility and probabilistic belief. The epistemic virtue was analyzed. The paper is the argument.
pmc-13458913: A 2026 editorial, "Beyond Classification," questioning diagnostic categories. The piece challenges the taxonomy. The editorial is the provocation.
pmc-13627113: A 2026 nationwide Korean cohort study on alcohol consumption's impact on hepatocellular carcinoma risk across age groups. The drinking-liver cancer link was age-stratified. The impact is the public health data.
pmc-13431013: In this 2026 Algerian study, diagnostic outcomes of the 2023 race-neutral versus 2012 race-specific GLI spirometry equations were compared in healthy adults (the title is truncated). The race-neutral equations were validated. The comparison matters for equity.
pmc-13364513: In this 2026 neuroimaging paper, high-resolution diffusion kurtosis imaging mapped hippocampus subfields across the healthy lifespan. The memory center's microstructure aged. The mapping is the normative resource.
pmc-13489713: This 2026 multilevel study examined involuntary retirement and organizational climates among older workers. The forced retirements' climates were compared. The study reveals the workplace dynamics.
pmc-13499113: This 2026 CML paper identified early predictors of MR4.5 attainment and eligibility for TKI discontinuation in patients on second-generation TKIs. The treatment-free remission predictors were found. The predictors guide stopping trials.
pmc-13446313: A 2026 paper showing a long first intron of PROS1 modulated protein S expression across tissues in mice and humans. The intron's regulatory role was discovered. The modulation is the genetic mechanism.
pmc-13526313: A 2026 case report of worm colic by massive biliary ascariasis. The intestinal worms invaded the bile ducts. The case is the dramatic reminder.
pmc-13427313: A 2026 paper on the SB Brasil Project — brief history and perspectives for the 2030 edition. Brazil's oral health survey was chronicled. The perspectives plan the future.

pmc-13528813: A 2026 Moroccan hospital laboratory study of the association between serum ferritin and glycated hemoglobin (the title is truncated). The iron-diabetes link was tested. The association is the clinical signal.
pmc-13426713: A 2026 paper on two cases of vallecular cyst — variable clinical presentation and management outcomes. The throat cysts' variety was documented. The cases guide ENT.

pmc-13461613: A 2026 case report of life-saving emergency chemotherapy in a critically ill patient with suspected metastatic testicular cancer prior to histological confirmation (the title is truncated). The empiric chemo saved the patient. The case is the dramatic lesson.
pmc-13420313: In this 2026 shrimp aquaculture paper, daily protein restriction under different protein levels was tested in whiteleg shrimp — growth, digestive system, gene expression, and health (the title is truncated). The protein regimes were compared. The testing informs feed.
arxiv-2606-16013: Multiple linear regression is one of the simplest statistical tools, and people trust it because it seems interpretable. This paper asks how far that trust should go: where exactly does interpretability break down, even in this easy case? The authors map the limits, giving data scientists a clearer sense of when "I can explain this model" stops being true.
arxiv-2606-16113: When an AI denies someone a loan or a job, the person deserves to know what would change the outcome — that's "algorithmic recourse." RecourseBench is a modular framework for testing recourse methods reproducibly, so researchers can compare them fairly. The paper presents the benchmark for the fairness-and-explainability research community.
arxiv-2606-16313: Self-driving cars predict where nearby vehicles will go, and rare, unusual trajectories (the "long tail") are where predictions fail dangerously. This paper asks whether trajectory displacement — how far a predicted path strays — is a safe measure in those rare cases. It targets autonomous-driving researchers worried about the edge cases that matter most.
arxiv-2606-16413: Imagine controlling a robot arm with your thoughts while seeing through its eyes in augmented reality. This paper builds a brain-robot interface with AR feedback for generalist robot-arm manipulation — one system handling many tasks. It targets researchers in brain-computer interfaces and assistive robotics.
arxiv-2606-16613: What brews when bot hordes swap, spar, and team up for the long haul? CoffeeBench drops long-game bot minds into mixed trade worlds — odd bots, odd jobs — and scores the brew. For herd-mind fans who watch bot bazaars bloom.
